title.narrative: Envelope 3: Emergency response for winter affected HHs in camps through integrated and dignified interventions

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtATAA Humanitarian Relief Association, as a pre-selected partner under Envelope 3 of the 2025 First Standard Allocation, is prepared to implement rapid, flexible humanitarian interventions in response to sudden displacement and return scenarios across Aleppo, Idleb, and Homs governorates. This envelope allows for pre-positioned funding to enable first-responder organizations to act immediately following crisis triggers such as conflict escalation, natural disasters, or mass returns.ltbrgtATAA has been selected based on its eligibility under the Syria Cross-border Humanitarian Fund (SCHF) and its demonstrated capacity to deliver integrated, multi-sector responses in volatile environments. With a strong operational presence in northern Syria and expanding access into central regions, ATAA can quickly reach crisis-affected populations, thanks to its established offices, mobile teams, and logistical readiness.ltbrgtThe proposed intervention is aligned with the contingency objectives outlined by OCHA. Once a crisis is identified and reported, the Humanitarian Financing Unit (HFU) will provide a decision within 48 hours to authorize activation of the response. ATAA will initiate field-level activities immediately and will submit an updated proposal with a full activity and budget plan within 20 working days, reflecting real-time needs assessments and contextual analysis.ltbrgtATAA’s response will cover a flexible mix of activities based on needs and operational feasibility. The core sectors of focus will include Protection, WASH, Shelter and Emergency NFI, and Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), while additional sectors may be integrated as required by the evolving situation.ltbrgtPlanned interventions may include:ltbrgtRapid deployment of field teams to assess needs and deliver essential services.ltbrgtProvision of emergency assistance through cash, in-kind, or service-based modalities, targeting newly displaced, returning families, or transit populations.ltbrgtEstablishment of service points or mobile units to address protection concerns, education continuity, or restoration of basic services.ltbrgtSupport to stabilize affected communities through emergency coordination, site management, or community-level engagement.ltbrgtCoordination with clusters, local authorities, and peer organizations to ensure effective, principled, and non-duplicative interventions.ltbrgtAll activities will be designed for rapid implementation and adapted to the scale and type of emergency. ATAA’s approach prioritizes inclusivity, gender sensitivity, and protection mainstreaming, with particular attention to persons with disabilities, women, children, and elderly populations. Accountability to affected populations (AAP) and community engagement will be integrated throughout the response cycle, including feedback and complaint mechanisms.ltbrgtATAA’s readiness to respond in Aleppo, Idleb, and Homs includes pre-positioned staff, community outreach structures, and established procurement and logistics pipelines. This capacity enables swift mobilization to any of the three governorates, regardless of the type or scope of the trigger. The organization’s flexible programming framework and field presence make it well-suited for contingency interventions that require speed, coverage, and adaptability.ltbrgtBy participating in this envelope, ATAA reaffirms its commitment to timely, coordinated humanitarian action that meets urgent needs and contributes to the stabilization of vulnerable communities impacted by new or renewed displacement in Syria.ltbrgtlt/pgt
